newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares set for more falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares set for more falls on profit-taking.

text.p: Danish share prices closed decidedly lower on Monday hit by massive profit-taking with dealers seeing more, if less dramatic declines ahead.

"There was across-the-board profit-taking, leading banks and A.P. Moeller were the worst affected. Tuesday will see more falls but nothing quite so major with the KFX index set to lose a half percentage point or so," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 3.50 point down at 154.39 in overall bourse turnover of 1.299 billion crowns. The KFX March future fell 3.60 point to 153.20 with 657 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
BG Bank closed 11 crowns lower at 299 after announcing 1996 results more or less in line with analyst expectations.
Top Danish banks Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark slipped on profit-taking, the former shedding 31 crowns to end at 587, the latter losing only two crowns to finish at 352.
Moeller's D/S 1912 dropped 9,000 crowns to 187,000 and D/S Svendborg 5,000 to 278,000, hit by the weaker dollar as well as profit-taking, as was Novo Nordisk which ended six down at 611.
